components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The default action for the next safe, intentional step.
components.css: .ds-button-primary { min-height: 34px; padding: 0 12px; border: 1px solid var(--accent); border-radius: var(--radius-sm); background: var(--accent); color: oklch(98% 0.005 285); font: 590 0.875rem/1.45 var(--font-ui); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 160ms cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1), border-color 160ms cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1); } .ds-button-primary:hover { background: var(--accent-hover); border-color: var(--accent-hover); } .ds-button-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-button-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A familiar neutral action that does not compete with the primary step.
components.css: .ds-button-secondary { min-height: 34px; padding: 0 12px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius-sm); background: var(--surface); color: var(--text); font: 590 0.875rem/1.45 var(--font-ui); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 160ms cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1), border-color 160ms cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1); } .ds-button-secondary:hover { border-color: var(--border-strong); background: var(--surface-raised); } .ds-button-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: A compact field for search, names, paths, and settings.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; height: 34px; padding: 0 10px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius-sm); background: var(--surface); color: var(--text); font: 400 0.875rem/1.45 var(--font-ui); } .ds-input:hover { border-color: var(--border-strong); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--text-faint); }

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: Compact text-backed status for unique, pending, failed, and complete states.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; min-height: 24px; padding: 0 7px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius-pill); background: var(--surface); color: var(--text-muted); font: 620 0.72rem/1.35 var(--font-ui); white-space: nowrap; } .ds-chip-success { background: var(--success-soft); color: var(--success); } .ds-chip-warning { background: var(--warning-soft); color: var(--warning); } .ds-chip-danger { background: var(--danger-soft); color: var(--danger); }

components.name: Navigation Item
components.description: A compact rail destination with a trailing count and quiet active state.
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; min-height: 36px; padding: 0 10px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--radius-sm); background: transparent; color: var(--text-muted); font: 400 0.875rem/1.45 var(--font-ui); text-decoration: none; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: var(--surface); color: var(--text); } .ds-nav-active { border-color: var(--border); background: var(--accent-soft); color: var(--text); } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-nav-count { color: var(--text-faint); font-size: 0.75rem; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Workbench Panel
components.description: A bordered, flat container for one coherent task or dataset.
components.html:
Current deployment

2 games selected, 0 files to remove.
components.css: .ds-panel { padding: 16px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius-md); background: var(--surface); color: var(--text); font-family: var(--font-ui); } .ds-panel h3 { margin: 0; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.35; } .ds-panel p { margin: 4px 0 0; max-width: 72ch; color: var(--text-muted); font-size: 0.76rem; line-height: 1.45; }

components.name: Mobile Library Record
components.description: The condensed phone representation of one ROM with one action entry point.
components.html: Pokemon Emerald Version (USA, Europe)GBA 16.0 MB · Unique
components.css: .ds-game-record { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 38px minmax(0,1fr) 44px; align-items: center; gap: 0; padding: 7px 8px; border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); border-radius: var(--radius-lg); background: var(--surface); color: var(--text); font-family: var(--font-ui); } .ds-game-record strong { display: -webkit-box; overflow: hidden; font-size: 0.9rem; line-height: 1.25; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; -webkit-line-clamp: 2; } .ds-game-record small { display: block; margin-top: 3px; color: var(--text-faint); font-size: 0.68rem; } .ds-game-record button { width: 44px; height: 44px; border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--radius-md); background: transparent; color: var(--text-muted); } .ds-game-record button:hover { border-color: var(--accent); color: var(--accent); } .ds-platform { padding: 2px 7px; border-radius: var(--radius-pill); background: var(--accent); color: oklch(98% 0.005 285); font-weight: 800; }

narrative.overview:
ROMmates is a focused workstation for people managing thousands of files, multiple handhelds, and filesystem operations with real consequences. The interface should feel like a well-organized workbench: dense without crowding, calm without becoming vague, and friendly without turning into a novelty. The name carries the joke. The interface earns trust.

The system is desktop-first because comparison, cleanup, and bulk operations benefit from width and density. The phone experience is not a reduced demo. It preserves every essential task through structural adaptation: the sidebar becomes a drawer, tables become compact records, secondary actions move into menus, and controls remain touch-friendly. Light and dark themes follow the operating system so the same restrained violet-tinted vocabulary works in a bright room or a dim one.

ROMmates explicitly rejects decorative retro-gaming launcher styling, arcade cabinet skins, generic card-heavy admin templates, and Finder's slow spatial file-browser feel. Information hierarchy, filenames, system state, and reversible consequences always outrank ornament.
keyCharacteristics: Restrained violet accent with explicit semantic state colors.
Gently rounded, consistently bordered controls and containers.
Compact rows on desktop, readable records on mobile.
Familiar controls that disappear into the task.

rules.name: The Consequence-First Rule
rules.body: The visual hierarchy must make pending additions, removals, conflicts, destructive actions, and recovery paths easier to see than decoration.

rules.name: The Structural Responsiveness Rule
rules.body: At 720px and below, restructure the interaction instead of merely shrinking it. At intermediate widths, wrap toolbars and simplify grids before content collides.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Violet is reserved for primary actions, current selection, focus, and actionable text. It must not become decorative wallpaper.

rules.name: The State Has Words Rule
rules.body: Success, warning, and danger colors must always be reinforced by text, an icon, or a recognizable state label. Color alone never carries meaning.

rules.name: The Theme Parity Rule
rules.body: Light and dark themes preserve the same hierarchy and semantics. Dark mode is not a separate neon aesthetic.

rules.name: The Filename Wins Rule
rules.body: Filenames and game titles receive the strongest weight in collection views. Metadata, paths, platform, and operational state step down in that order.

rules.name: The Two-Line Limit Rule
rules.body: Mobile game titles may use at most two lines. Supporting metadata stays on one compact wrapping row, and long paths use ellipsis or intentional wrapping according to context.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-Temporary Rule
rules.body: Persistent page structure uses borders and tonal layers. Shadows are reserved for temporary overlays or a control actively floating above content.

rules.name: The Single Surface Rule
rules.body: Never nest a decorative card inside another decorative card. Use dividers, rows, and spacing inside a container.

dos: Do optimize for scanning thousands of filenames: compact rows, sticky headings, indexed search, filters, and bulk actions.
Do use the shared radius scale for every fully bordered control or container.
Do keep the violet accent rare enough that primary actions and current selection remain obvious.
Do preview filesystem consequences before rename, trash, restore, deployment, clone, or group synchronization operations.
Do make destructive operations recoverable and show where the recovery path lives.
Do preserve complete functionality on mobile through drawers, record layouts, action menus, and 44px touch targets.
Do test new pages at 1440px, 1024px, 768px, and 390px before shipping.
Do use semantic controls, visible focus, non-color labels, and WCAG 2.1 AA contrast as the baseline.
Do use the filesystem as operational truth while presenting database-backed intent and ownership clearly.
donts: Don't resemble a decorative retro-gaming launcher or an arcade cabinet skin.
Don't build a generic card-heavy admin template. A row or divider is usually enough.
Don't recreate Finder's slow spatial file browser with folders as the primary discovery model.
Don't use oversized dashboard metrics. Collection health must remain proportional to the work around it.
Don't use ornamental game imagery when it competes with filenames, state, or actions.
Don't hide destructive behavior or collapse consequences into vague confirmation copy.
Don't use playful styling that competes with filenames and operational status. The ROMmates name supplies the personality.
Don't use sharp bordered rectangles beside rounded components. The shared radius tokens are mandatory.
Don't allow text, menus, tables, or toolbars to create page-level horizontal overflow.
Don't use gradient text, glassmorphism, colored side-stripe borders, decorative motion, or bounce easing.
Don't invent a new button, chip, input, or card vocabulary for one screen. Extend the central system instead.
Don't rely on color alone for success, warning, danger, ownership, selection, or connectivity.
